metadata.case_name: MUNG YEE KI v. CHUNG NING

injuries.description: CT scan of the head showed comminuted depressed frontal skull vault fracture and skull base fracture involving the orbits, frontal sinus and fractures of the left temporal bone and zygoma as well.
injuries.body_part: frontal skull vault, skull base, orbits, left temporal bone, zygoma
source: CT scan of the head showed comminuted depressed frontal skull vault fracture and skull base fracture involving the orbits, frontal sinus and fractures of the left temporal bone and zygoma as well.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple fractures involving skull or facial bones

injuries.description: Epidural haematoma over the frontal region
source: Subsequently, the plaintiff suffered epidural haematoma over the frontal region, traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage and pneumoencephaly.

injuries.description: Fracture of orbits and traumatic optic neuropathy with significant visual impairment
source: Amongst other injuries, the plaintiff suffered a fracture of orbits and traumatic optic neuropathy in the traffic accident on 8 December 2000 and is still attending regular follow up treatment at the Department of Ophthalmology of Caritas Medical Centre every three months.

Combining the disability in all aspects of visual function, the plaintiff suffers from 42% impairment of the whole visual system which is a 40% impairment of the whole person according to the AMA Guide.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of eye or orbit

injuries.description: The left index finger extensor tendon was partially cut.
source: The left index finger extensor tendon was partially cut.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration of extensor muscle, fascia or tendon of other finger at wrist or hand level

injuries.description: Multiple lacerations over the forehead, right shoulder, right hand, left thumb, index and middle fingers resulting in permanent scarring
injuries.body_part: forehead, right shoulder, right hand, left thumb/index/middle fingers
source: Upon admission, he was confused and found to have suffered multiple lacerations over the forehead, right shoulder, right hand, left thumb, index and middle fingers.
There are readily noticeable pale accident scars over much of his forehead.

injuries.description: Panhypopituitarism and Cranial Diabetes Insipidus (endocrine dysfunction) requiring lifelong hormonal replacement
source: The plaintiff developed Hypopituitarism and Cranial Diabetes Insipidus within days of the accident as can be seen from the reports of the Government hospitals.

The government medical reports show that the plaintiff requires medication for the treatment of hypofunction of the adrenal glands, thyroid, testes and posterior pituitary (known as Cranial Diabetes Insipidus).
The plaintiff will need lifelong hormonal replacement as recovery is very unusual.

injuries.description: Epidural abscess, osteomyelitis and wound dehiscence of the skull, chronic skull bone infection requiring removal of affected bone
source: On 9 March 2001 the plaintiff was admitted to Princess Margaret Hospital for complaint of intermittent purulent discharge from his forehead wound. CT scan showed a collection over the epidural space together with intracranial air. The diagnosis was epidural abscess, osteomyelitis and wound dehiscene.
Still later, the plaintiff further suffered from chronic skull bone infection and was arranged to receive surgery to remove all affected bone and to receive antimicrobial therapy.

injuries.description: Persistent skull deformity (forehead depressed due to underlying frontal sinus fracture and previous cranioplasty)
source: The plaintiff had persistent skull deformity. His forehead was depressed due to the underlying frontal sinus fracture and previous cranioplasty.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of squama of frontal bone of skull

injuries.description: Harvest of ribs and free Latissimus Dorsi flap for skull reconstruction with resultant scar on back and weakened ability to pull
injuries.body_part: left chest / back (latissimus dorsi) and chest wall (ribs)
source: The skull defect was reconstructed by ribs harvested from the chest and the soft tissue coverage was achieved by a free Latissimus Dorsi flap. After the operation, the plaintiff was left with scars on his back and his ability to pull is weakened because the muscle was harvested for reconstruction.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of other specified muscle, fascia, tendon or bursa at shoulder or upper arm level

injuries.description: Very severe head injury resulting in dementia due to head trauma, global cognitive dysfunction and psychiatric illness (Depressive Disorder and PTSD)
source: The Dementia due to Head Trauma is shown by the plaintiff’s impairment of memory and executive functioning which results from very severe head injury from the accident and is mild to moderate in degree in that work and social activities are impaired but the capacity for independent living largely remains.
In their joint report, they made the finding that the plaintiff was suffering from (1) Depressive Disorder; (2) Post-traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD); and (3) Dementia due to Head Trauma.

manifestations.description: Poor vision of his left eye
Impairment of left eye extraocular movements
Headaches mainly at the left frontal region occurring two to three times a week and lasting for two to three hours each time
Diplopia at the extremes of lateral gaze horizontally
Depressive mood, lack of interests, energy and motivation, sleep impairment, retardation, restlessness, and feelings of worthlessness (Depressive Disorder)

Features of personality change: feelings of inadequacy, social ineptness and hypersensitivity, sense of humiliation and discrimination, fear of embarrassment, ridicule, criticism and rejection with consequent avoidance of social activities and interpersonal relationships

Post-traumatic symptoms: nightmares, flashbacks, avoidance of stimuli associated with the accident, numbing of general responsiveness, increased arousal (sleep impairment, irritability, reduced interests)
Photophobia due to mildly dilated left pupil; advised to wear sunglasses
Generalized visual field constriction in both eyes and defective colour vision (more profound in the left eye)
Loss of libido, masculinity and infertility due to gonadal hormone deficiency
Persistent CSF leakage from the nose and the right ear (healed with conservative management)
Right hand dorsum ulceration requiring splintage

treatments_received: Taken by ambulance to Princess Margaret Hospital
Exploration of the forehead wound and surgical toilet
Craniotomy and evacuation of the epidural haematoma and fixation of the skull bone fragments by mini-plates
Reopening of the craniotomy and left orbitotomy as well as decompression and repair of dural tear
Wound debridement and rotational flap and free skin graft from the left side of his neck
Craniectomy and removal of necrotic bone and plates and drainage of the epidural abscess
Insertion of subclavian line and prolonged course of antibiotics
Reconstruction surgery with ribs harvested from the chest and free Latissimus Dorsi flap
treatments_future: Lifelong endocrinologist consultations and lifelong hormonal replacement (testosterone, hydrocortisone, thyroxine, desmopressin)
Possible future Growth Hormone replacement (assessed as a high chance of future requirement)
Infertility treatment with hormones (estimated cost allowed)
Psychotherapy and medication for psychiatric condition (treatment period estimated in report)
Travel for future treatment and consultations

losses.description: Readily noticeable pale accident scars over much of his forehead, a conspicuous light brown raised slightly bulbous patch of skin flap on the left forehead, scars on nose and ear region, scars on back from flap harvest and several healed laceration scars on hands; cosmetic disability assessed as permanent by Dr Nicolson.
Global cognitive dysfunction and dementia due to head trauma causing impairment of memory and executive functioning.
Personality change in reaction to disfigurement with feelings of inadequacy, social ineptness, hypersensitivity, humiliation and avoidance of social activities; assessed as severe in degree.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Persistent avoidance of minibuses, going out alone and avoidance of conversations about the accident due to PTSD and related psychological consequences.
Avoidance of social activities and interpersonal relationships as a consequence of psychiatric conditions and disfigurement.

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: Gonadal hormone deficiency resulting in loss of libido, masculinity and infertility; infertility treatment cost allowed.
Persistent skull deformity (depressed forehead) and resultant physical alteration to skull and chest due to reconstruction (rib harvest and latissimus dorsi flap) with weakened ability to pull.
Handicap in the labour market and inability to pursue intended career as a designer due to combined disabilities (neurological, psychiatric, visual and endocrine).
